open_item_note: PI-Q263-COLLISION was not addressed in the 2026-09-17 directives and remains open. It is not marked resolved here, because an unruled item recorded as settled is how a decision quietly goes missing.
purpose: Every decision that is the PI's to make, in one place. Each item names the question, what it blocks, and where the full reasoning lives.
this_file_is_an_index: The authoritative record for each item is the file named in `detail_record`. Decisions are written there too, so the two cannot drift apart.

executed: Applied to the 2 BCE facts in the corpus: BCSGK-0125 (খ্রিষ্টপূর্ব ১৫০০ অব্দ) and BCSGK-0142 (খ্রিষ্টপূর্ব ৩২১ অব্দ). Both already had all numeric temporal fields null, so no invented date had to be removed; the notes were added.
ruling: Do not invent invalid ISO strings. Preserve the raw text date in `temporal_evidence_notes` and keep the numeric temporal fields null, so strict JSON schema validity holds and no parser breaks.
seed_exception: BCSGK-0142 is in the frozen seed. The seed file was NOT edited: its copy already satisfies the ruling substantively (numerics null). Adding the note there would change the seed sha256 in model_b_release_manifest.json and require a re-freeze. Flagged for the PI rather than done unilaterally.
title: BCE dates cannot be expressed in the current schema

consequence_recorded: BCSGK-0336 is now permanently unusable as worded: five independent claims in one row, no admissible pre-cutoff source for any of them, and no route to decomposition. This is the accepted cost of ID integrity, not an open task.
ruling: Rule 11 enforced strictly. Compound rows are NOT split and no new fact_uid is created. A compound row that cannot be verified by a single atomic evidence excerpt stays at partial_support or excluded.
title: Whether a compound row may be split into separate facts
